archetype.name: Overachiever (pitching-first)
archetype.definition: A team whose run margin pointed to about 82 wins took the AL Central and reached the ALCS behind a top-tier staff and a bottom-tier lineup.

report.headline: A run-prevention team squeezed a division and an ALCS trip from little offense

recap.finish: 85-77, won the AL Central; beat CHW 3-2 in the ALDS, lost the ALCS 2-4 to TB
recap.body:
This was Cleveland in its familiar shape. The staff's 3.77 ERA ranked 8th, well under the league's 4.173, and allowed runs per game ranked 8th as well. The lineup's .696 OPS ranked 26th and runs per game ranked 24th, with the hitters graded D+ against a B+ rotation and a B bullpen. The full-season margin was thin: 678 runs scored, 667 allowed, a +11 differential that implies 82.2 wins. Cleveland won 85 and took the division over Chicago, 85-77 to 84-78.

The season zigzagged before it surged. A 16-16 start became 34-27 after an 18-11 May. Then the offense fell away: a 10-15 June at 3.48 runs a game and a 12-13 July left the team at 56-55. August was a 13-13 holding pattern. The bats finally showed up in September, 4.84 runs a game in a 16-9 month, and the team closed 8-2 over its last ten. That run included 1-0 wins over the Athletics and Red Sox, the kind of games this roster was built to win.

The rotation carried the year. Parker Messick was the ace: a 2.56 ERA and 4.9 WAR across 186.1 innings. Gavin Williams struck out 33.2% of batters, with 248 strikeouts and a 3.47 FIP. Foster Griffin and Joey Cantillo kept their ERAs near 3.6. Only Tanner Bibee, who threw the most innings, lagged, with a 4.36 ERA and 4.52 FIP. Cade Smith closed with 41 saves, a 1.95 ERA and a 36.3% strikeout rate, 7th on the reliever tab. The lineup's value came from table-setting and gloves rather than power: Steven Kwan (114 wRC+, .382 OBP), Chase DeLauter (131 wRC+), Brayan Rocchio (9.4 Def Runs) and All-Star Travis Bazzana. Meanwhile Jo Adell took the most plate appearances, 660, for a 96 wRC+ and 0.6 WAR. José Ramírez stole 37 bases but hit for only a 92 wRC+.

October followed the same script. Down 0-2 at home to the White Sox after scoring three runs in two games, Cleveland won three straight, scoring nine in each road game and then closing it 2-0. Against Tampa Bay it took Game 1 7-3 and Game 3 3-2, then lost the last three games, scoring 3, 1 and 3. Williams was overpowering, striking out 51.6% of hitters, and Smith allowed almost nothing. But outside Ramírez (168 wRC+), DeLauter and Patrick Bailey, the lineup stopped producing: Rocchio posted a -1 wRC+, Angel Martínez -37, Kwan 62. A lineup that can't produce runs gives its pitchers no slack in a seven-game series.

The bigger pattern is the one in history. This is the fourth time in five years that W vs Run Diff came out positive, including a 7.7 in 2025. Offense has ranked 24th or worse in three of the last four seasons, while run prevention has ranked 8th or better in every year since 2022. The formula keeps producing winning records and division-level seasons. It keeps running out of runs when the games get tight.

highlights.title: Messick and Williams fronted elite rotation
highlights.body: Messick's 2.56 ERA and 4.9 WAR made him one of the league's best starters at 15th on the tab, and Williams' strikeout rate was the best on the staff by a wide margin. With Griffin and Cantillo solid behind them, four of the five starters kept their ERAs under 3.8, which is why the B+ grade held up across nearly 900 innings. FIP backs the top two, so this looks repeatable rather than lucky.

highlights.title: Cade Smith locked down the ninth
highlights.body: Smith converted 41 saves with a 1.95 ERA and a 2.18 FIP. That made him the 7th-ranked reliever on the site, and he carried it into October with a 0.87 ERA. The rest of the bullpen was average-to-good rather than dominant, so much of the B grade runs through him.

highlights.title: September surge sealed the division
highlights.body: At 69-68 after August, the division was still open. A 16-9 September, with the offense at its best of the year, and an 8-2 finish pushed Cleveland past the White Sox by a single game. The late scoring was real but short-lived: in the playoffs the bats went quiet again.

lowlights.title: A bottom-tier offense, again
lowlights.body: The .696 OPS ranked 26th and the team scored 0.29 runs a game below the league. The hitters grade was a D+, and a pitcher-friendly park explains only part of that. Adell's heavy playing time at a 96 wRC+ with -6.3 Def Runs, and weak first-base production from Lowe and Manzardo, dragged on the group. Given 2023 and 2025 looked the same, this is structural, not a slump.

lowlights.title: Record outran the run margin
lowlights.body: A +11 differential implies 82.2 wins, and Cleveland won 85 on a +2.8 W vs Run Diff, a habit it also showed with 7.7 in 2025. Winning close games is partly a bullpen skill when Smith is closing. But a team living this near .500 on margin is one bad break from a losing record.

lowlights.title: ALCS bats went silent late
lowlights.body: After a 2-1 lead over Tampa Bay, Cleveland lost three straight and scored three runs or fewer in each. Rocchio, Martínez and Kwan combined for almost nothing at the plate in October. The pitching kept series close, but the lineup couldn't hold up its end.

arc.note: A strong May gave way to a June-July slide that dropped the team to 56-55, before a 16-9 September and an 8-2 finish won the division. In October the team came back from 0-2 against Chicago, then lost the last three ALCS games to Tampa Bay.

recap.nextYear: The pitching is the asset that carries forward. Messick and Williams pitched like a front two with FIP to match, Griffin and Cantillo were solid, and Smith anchored the bullpen. Bibee's 4.36 ERA and 4.52 FIP make him the rotation spot most open to improvement. The offense is where the work is. The D+ group got real value from Kwan, DeLauter, Rocchio and Bazzana, but the heaviest playing time went to Adell at 0.6 WAR. First base produced little between Lowe and Manzardo, and Ramírez's 92 wRC+ left the middle of the order without its anchor. The record also leaned on close-game results for a second straight year. With a differential that implies roughly 82 wins, repeating 85 isn't guaranteed unless the lineup closes some of the gap to the league."

confidence.note: Full 162-game season plus two playoff series; postseason splits are small samples.
